subject: psychology

provenance.source: https://docs.aglasem.com/view/81bd948e-c701-11f1-aa04-0aa932765c8b (AglaSem Docs copy of the NTA master question paper, downloaded 22 Nov 2026 with the owner's approval); text in data/coverage/cuet2026/psychology-paper.json
provenance.keySource: NTA CUET (UG) 2026 final answer key, option ids; all 50 questions authenticated by question id and option id (data/coverage/cuet2026/psychology-ids.json)

bankRead: One read-only read on 22 Nov 2026 with the repo read script (SELECT only): 161 visible psychology rows saved in tmp/1122-coverage/snap/psychology/bank_psychology.json; the repo's practice-eligibility check kept 145 served rows (served_psychology.json, served_rows.json), matching the stored inventory count of 145. 16 visible rows were not eligible and were not used. Eligibility output in eligible.txt.
keyCardDeck: data/keycards/decks/psychology.json (826 cards across the 7 syllabus chapters; the card-suspension table was not read in this run, to keep to one read)
syllabusSource: data/cuet_syllabus.js psychology (7 chapters); every question sits on the 2026 syllabus
method: data/coverage/METHOD.md (STRICT rule; doubtful = not covered; Key cards count for theory). Fact lists written first in tmp/1122-coverage/snap/psychology/facts_before_search.json, then searched with tmp/1122-coverage/snap/psychology/s.mjs; this file built by build_A.mjs there, which checks every cited id is served or in the deck.
paperStructure: One group of 50 numbered questions (451 to 500): 40 single questions and two five-question comprehension sets (Seema, Q491-495; Abby, Q496-500). No numerical items.

facts: Intelligence is the global capacity to understand the world, think rationally and use resources effectively when faced with challenges (Wechsler)

matches.teaches: intelligence = global capacity to understand the world, think rationally, use resources effectively

questions.reason: Key card states the definition word for word.

facts: Alfred Binet was one of the first psychologists to work on intelligence (first intelligence test)

matches.teaches: Binet was one of the first psychologists who worked on intelligence
Binet developed the first intelligence test

questions.reason: Key card says Binet was one of the first psychologists to work on intelligence; the bank item adds that he built the first test.

facts: Guilford structure-of-intellect: operations dimension has 6 factors (key says 6)

matches.teaches: the six operations: cognition, memory recording, memory retention, divergent production, convergent production, evaluation
three dimensions: operations, contents, products
dimensions are operations, contents, products

questions.reason: Key card names all six operations of the model, so the count of six is read straight off the list (the number itself is not printed; this is the thinnest covered call of the set).

facts: Gardner's intelligences: musical, spatial, logical-mathematical (and linguistic, bodily-kinaesthetic, interpersonal, intrapersonal, naturalistic)
Componential is Sternberg's analytical intelligence, not Gardner's

matches.teaches: Gardner's eight intelligences listed; componential belongs to Sternberg
linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, musical, bodily-kinaesthetic, interpersonal, intrapersonal, naturalistic

questions.reason: Bank item asks which type is not Gardner's and its explanation names all eight and puts componential with Sternberg; the card lists the eight.

facts: Sternberg: creative intelligence = experiential intelligence

matches.teaches: experiential or creative intelligence
componential, experiential, contextual

questions.reason: Key card states experiential and creative intelligence are the same component.

facts: Identical twins reared apart: intelligence correlation about 0.72
questions.reason: Nothing served states the 0.72 correlation for identical twins reared apart (no twin-study material in the bank or the deck).

facts: Intellectual disability IQ ranges: mild 55-70; moderate 35-40 to 50-55; severe 20-25 to 35-40; profound below 20-25

matches.teaches: mild 55-70; moderate 35-40 to 50-55; severe 20-25 to 35-40; profound below 20-25

questions.reason: Key card gives all four levels with their IQ ranges, which is the whole match.

facts: Gifted children: advanced logical thinking and problem solving, preference for solitary academic work, superior generalisation and discrimination
Gifted children have HIGH intrinsic motivation and good self-esteem (low is not a characteristic)

matches.teaches: advanced logical thinking and problem solving, superior generalisation and discrimination, high intrinsic motivation and self-esteem, preference for solitary academic activity

questions.reason: Key card lists the characteristics, including high intrinsic motivation and self-esteem, so the low-motivation option is the one gifted children do not have.

facts: Indian verbal tests: Bihar Test of Intelligence (Mohsin), Group Test of General Mental Ability (Jalota), Test of General Mental Ability (Joshi)
Draw-a-Man (Pramila Pathak) is a nonverbal/performance test

matches.teaches: verbal tests need verbal responses (general only)

questions.reason: The cards define verbal and performance tests but no served item names the Indian tests (Bihar Test, Group Test of General Mental Ability, Joshi's test) or says Draw-a-Man is non-verbal.

facts: Self-concept = the way we perceive ourselves and the ideas we hold about our competencies and attributes

matches.teaches: self-concept = how we perceive ourselves and our ideas about our competencies and attributes

questions.reason: Key card states the definition word for word.

facts: Self-efficacy = belief that one has the ability/behaviours required by a situation (Bandura)

matches.teaches: belief that one has the ability or behaviours required by a situation = high self-efficacy
self-efficacy (Bandura) vs self-esteem and self-regulation

questions.reason: Key card states it word for word; the bank item separates self-efficacy from self-esteem and self-regulation.

facts: Personality has physical and psychological components
Personality is dynamic: some features may change with situational demands
Personality expression in behaviour is fairly unique to the individual
Personality does not change easily (relatively stable)

matches.teaches: physical and psychological components; unique expression; main features do not easily change; dynamic

questions.reason: Key card lists the four features, so A, C and D are right and B (changes easily) is wrong.

facts: Hippocrates humoral types: sanguine, phlegmatic, choleric, melancholic
Endomorphic is Sheldon's body type (not Hippocrates)

matches.teaches: sanguine, phlegmatic, melancholic, choleric
endomorphic, mesomorphic, ectomorphic are Sheldon's

questions.reason: Key card lists Hippocrates' four types; the Sheldon card places endomorphic with body-build types.

facts: Type D personality is prone to depression/distress (negative affectivity, social inhibition)

matches.teaches: Type-D personality is characterised by proneness to depression

questions.reason: Key card states it word for word.

facts: Freud used hypnosis, free association and dream analysis
Fictional finalism is Adler's idea, not a Freud method

matches.teaches: free association, dream analysis, analysis of errors

questions.reason: The Key card lists free association and dream analysis but not hypnosis, and nothing says fictional finalism is Adler's, so hypnosis versus fictional finalism cannot be settled from served material.

facts: Channelling sexual/aggressive energy into socially accepted activity (religious fervour) = sublimation (textbook); NTA key says reaction formation (disputable)

matches.teaches: adopting behaviours opposite to one's true feelings

questions.reason: The NTA key (reaction formation) conflicts with the textbook idea of channelling urges into a worthy activity; the served card defines reaction formation as the opposite behaviour, which does not fit the case, and no served item teaches sublimation. Not closable by adding material.

facts: Jodhpur Multiphasic Personality Inventory was developed by Mallick and Joshi

matches.teaches: JMPI developed by Mallick and Joshi

questions.reason: Key card states who developed the JMPI.

facts: Inkblot test - Rorschach
Picture-Frustration Study - Rosenzweig
Thematic Apperception Test - Morgan and Murray
16 PF - Cattell

matches.teaches: Inkblot test developed by Rorschach
Picture-Frustration Study developed by Rosenzweig
TAT developed by Morgan and Murray
16PF developed by Cattell

questions.reason: Four separate Key cards name the developer of each of the four tests in the list, so every pair is taught.

facts: MMPI and Eysenck Personality Questionnaire are self-report measures
Picture-Frustration Study and Sentence Completion Test are projective, not self-report

matches.teaches: self-report measures defined (no examples)
Picture-Frustration Study (projective)
sentence completion

questions.reason: No served answer side says that MMPI and EPQ are self-report measures while the Picture-Frustration Study and Sentence Completion are projective; only card tags link them.

facts: A moderate level of stress is suitable for optimal performance (eustress)

matches.teaches: eustress is the level of stress that is good for you

questions.reason: Served material names eustress as good stress but never says a moderate level gives optimal performance.

facts: In stress the adrenal gland releases catecholamines (adrenaline and noradrenaline) into the bloodstream

matches.teaches: adrenal gland releases large amounts of catecholamines into the blood stream

questions.reason: Key card states the sentence the item completes.

facts: Dimensions of stress: intensity, duration, complexity, predictability, uncontrollability (and the keyed 'controllability' is not listed)

matches.teaches: dimensions: intensity, duration, complexity, predictability

questions.reason: Key card lists the four dimensions; complexity, predictability and duration are in it and controllability is not.

facts: Selye GAS alarm reaction: stressor activates the adrenal-pituitary-cortex system

matches.teaches: alarm reaction: stressor activates the adrenal-pituitary-cortex system

questions.reason: Key card states it for the alarm reaction stage.

facts: Stress impairs immune function and can cause illness
Stress affects natural killer cell cytotoxicity
Stress hormones weaken the immune system and affect physical and mental health
Optimal stress does not always enhance immune function (D false)

matches.teaches: stress affects natural killer cell cytotoxicity (B)
effects of stress on the immune system
chronic stress weakens immune functioning; stress hormones suppress immune responses (A and C)

questions.reason: A, B and C are taught, but nothing says statement D (optimal stress always strengthens immunity) is false, so the choice between options 2 and 4 is not settled.

facts: Hardiness personality trait was given by Kobasa

matches.teaches: Kobasa: personality traits of hardiness
commitment, control, challenge

questions.reason: Key card ties hardiness to Kobasa.

facts: Four Ds of abnormality: deviance, distress, dysfunction, danger

matches.teaches: deviance, distress, dysfunction, danger
each D explained

questions.reason: Key card names the four Ds.

facts: ICD-10 is prepared by the World Health Organisation (DSM is by American Psychiatric Association)

matches.teaches: ICD-10 prepared by the World Health Organisation
DSM is by the American Psychiatric Association

questions.reason: Key card says WHO prepared ICD-10 and the APA publishes DSM.

facts: Low GABA activity is linked to anxiety disorders

matches.teaches: low GABA activity linked to anxiety disorders

questions.reason: Key card states it word for word.

facts: Ellis RET A-B-C = Antecedent, Belief, Consequence

matches.teaches: first step in RET is the antecedent-belief-consequence (ABC) analysis
irrational beliefs mediate between antecedent events and consequences

questions.reason: Key card spells out ABC as antecedent-belief-consequence.

facts: Ethical standards for therapists: confidentiality, informed consent, respect for human rights and dignity, goal of alleviating distress and suffering

matches.teaches: informed consent, confidentiality, alleviating distress, integrity, respect for human rights and dignity

questions.reason: Key card lists the ethical standards and includes all four statements A to D.

facts: Features/properties of attitudes: valence, extremeness, simplicity or complexity (multiplexity), centrality
Motivation is not a property of attitude

matches.teaches: valence, extremeness, simplicity or complexity (multiplexity), centrality

questions.reason: Key card lists the four features; motivation is not one of them.

facts: Heider P-O-X: balance when all three sides positive, or two negative and one positive
Imbalance when all three negative, or two positive and one negative

matches.teaches: balance: all three positive, or two negative and one positive
imbalance: all three negative, or two positive and one negative

questions.reason: The two Key cards give both halves of the rule, so all four statements are checked.

facts: Cognitive dissonance was proposed by Leon Festinger

matches.teaches: cognitive dissonance proposed by Leon Festinger

questions.reason: Key card states it word for word.

facts: Attitude components ABC: affective = feeling, behavioural = action tendency, cognitive = belief/view
Order requested: cognitive, behavioural, affective

matches.teaches: belief = cognitive, liking = affective, behaviour = behavioural component; ABC model
cognitive, affective, behavioural aspects
feeling sad and angry at trees being cut = affective

questions.reason: Bank item sorts a belief, a feeling and an action into the three components, the same steps with a different example; the card confirms feeling is the affective part.

facts: Mohsin proposed the two-step (two-stage) concept of attitude change

matches.teaches: two-step concept proposed by S. M. Mohsin

questions.reason: Key card states it word for word.

facts: Group formation stages in order: forming, storming, norming, performing, adjourning

matches.teaches: forming, storming, norming, performing, adjourning
forming, storming, norming, performing in order

questions.reason: Key card gives the five stages in order; the bank item asks the same ordering.

facts: Draw-a-Man - Pramila Pathak
Bihar Test of Intelligence - Mohsin
Test of General Mental Ability (Hindi) - Joshi
Group Test of Intelligence - Prayag Mehta
questions.reason: No served item pairs the Indian intelligence tests (Draw-a-Man, Bihar Test, Test of General Mental Ability in Hindi, Group Test of Intelligence) with Pathak, Mohsin, Joshi and Mehta.

facts: Bandwagon effect: feeling one's view is validated when others share it / going with the crowd

matches.teaches: finding others favour capital punishment validates the view: bandwagon effect

questions.reason: Key card states the same example and names it the bandwagon effect.

facts: Social loafing: members feel less responsible for the overall task and exert less effort

matches.teaches: reduction in individual effort on a collective task
when effort cannot be identified members relax and become free riders
loafing falls when each member's contribution is identifiable

questions.reason: Cards give the meaning and the cause (effort cannot be identified, so members ease off), and the bank item shows individual evaluation reduces it, which rules out the other three options; the wording "feel less responsible" is not printed.

facts: Conditions for group formation: proximity, similarity, common motives and goals
Individual goals are not a condition

matches.teaches: proximity, similarity, common motives and goals

questions.reason: Key card lists the conditions; individual goals is not among them.

facts: OCD: obsessions (intrusive recurrent thoughts) and compulsions (repetitive acts such as hand washing) causing anxiety, interfering with normal life

matches.teaches: OCD: preoccupation with specific ideas and repeated acts that affect normal activities
compulsions include washing

questions.reason: Key card describes the disorder almost in the passage's own terms, so the student must know it to name it (the passage does not name it, so this is not a reading item).

facts: Obsession = persistence of unwanted thought or idea that cannot be stopped

matches.teaches: obsessive behaviour is the inability to stop thinking about a particular idea or topic

questions.reason: Key card states it word for word.

facts: Compulsion = repetitive behaviour/act performed to reduce anxiety from intrusive thoughts

matches.teaches: compulsive behaviour is the need to perform certain behaviours over and over again
repeatedly carrying out an act or series of acts

questions.reason: Key card separates obsessive thinking from compulsive repeated behaviour, which is what the item asks about the repeated act.

facts: OCD and related disorders: hoarding disorder, trichotillomania, excoriation (skin-picking) disorder
Conversion disorder is a somatic symptom/dissociative disorder, not OCRD

matches.teaches: conversion disorder is a somatic symptom disorder

questions.reason: Conversion disorder is taught as a somatic symptom disorder, but no served item says hoarding, trichotillomania and excoriation are the obsessive-compulsive and related disorders.

facts: Trichotillomania = hair-pulling disorder
questions.reason: Nothing served says trichotillomania is hair-pulling; the word does not appear in the bank or the deck.

facts: Behaviour therapy techniques: token economy, modelling, systematic desensitisation, aversive conditioning, differential reinforcement, flooding
Cognitive restructuring belongs to cognitive therapy

matches.teaches: token economy is a behaviour technique
modelling in behaviour therapy
systematic desensitisation and aversive conditioning as behaviour techniques
cognitive restructuring is the aim of Beck's cognitive therapy

questions.reason: Cards and a bank item place token economy, modelling and systematic desensitisation in behaviour therapy and cognitive restructuring in Beck's cognitive therapy.

facts: Systematic desensitisation was developed by Wolpe

matches.teaches: systematic desensitisation developed by Joseph Wolpe
Wolpe - systematic desensitisation

questions.reason: Bank item asks the same thing with the same answer.

facts: Differential reinforcement reduces unwanted behaviour and increases wanted behaviour at the same time

matches.teaches: reduces unwanted and increases wanted behaviour simultaneously
two methods

questions.reason: Key card states the sentence the item describes.

facts: Vicarious learning / modelling: learning by observing others; gradual acquisition of model's behaviour through rewarding small changes (key: vicarious learning)

matches.teaches: vicarious learning: learning by observing others, rewarding small changes in behaviour

questions.reason: Key card states it word for word.

facts: Aversive conditioning is used for alcohol addiction

matches.teaches: aversive conditioning used for an alcoholic (shock paired with smell of alcohol)
repeated association of undesired response with an aversive consequence

questions.reason: Key card gives alcohol addiction as the worked case for aversive conditioning.
